alt: Six causes of rising greenhouse gas concentrations linked to the gas each releases. Fossil fuel combustion, deforestation, cement manufacture and increasing population and energy use add carbon dioxide; agriculture and changes in land use such as draining wetlands add methane.
caption: Learn each cause with its gas: four add carbon dioxide, two add methane.

alt: Left: solar radiation reaches the Earth’s surface; radiation from the surface is absorbed by a layer of greenhouse gases and re-emitted back down, while some escapes. Right: higher gas concentrations lead to global warming, which leads to climate change. Below: the definition of a greenhouse gas and the three named gases.
caption: Keep the order: more gas, then global warming, then climate change.

alt: Climate change branches into three groups of impacts. Physical changes: warmer land and ocean surfaces, melting ice and rising sea level, ocean acidification and more extreme weather. Effects on living things: disrupted food chains, biodiversity change, habitat loss, forced migration, pests and invasive species. Effects on food: changing crop yields and food shortages.
caption: Group the twelve impacts, then link them as cause and effect in longer answers.

alt: Cross-section of land carrying an ice sheet beside the ocean. Meltwater from the land ice flows into the sea and warmer water expands, so sea level rises from a dashed earlier line to a higher line. Floating sea ice sits in the water and is marked as not significantly raising sea level.
caption: Sea level rises from melting land ice and expanding warmer water, not from melting sea ice.

alt: The twelve named strategies in four groups. Use less fossil energy: reduced fossil fuel use, energy efficiency, transport policies, fewer children per woman. Cut farm emissions: sustainable food choices, less livestock farming. Take carbon dioxide out of the air: reforestation and afforestation, carbon sequestration. Steer and plan: international agreements, taxation, research and climate models, AI.
caption: Grouping the twelve strategies by what they do makes them easier to recall and explain.

alt: A chain from emissions to more greenhouse gases, global warming and climate change impacts. Reducing carbon footprints acts at the start of the chain; adaptation acts at the end. Below are the four adaptation strategies: resistant crops, better flood defences, legislation on building in risky areas, and building design.
caption: Footprint strategies reduce the cause; adaptation strategies reduce the harm.

after: ## Worked example 1: a carbon footprint calculation
alt: Bar chart of yearly carbon dioxide from travel. Before: 2,700 kg, all from the car. After switching 40% of journeys to the bus: 1,620 kg from the car plus 300 kg from the bus, 1,920 kg in total, a saving of 780 kg or 28.9%. The working is listed beside the chart.
caption: Work out each part, add them, then find the saving as a percentage of the original.
